prompt: Customers receive an email when a product they subscribed to becomes available again.

intent.desiredOutcome: Customers receive an email when a product they subscribed to becomes available again.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version handles edge cases: suppressing duplicate emails if inventory fluctuates, cleaning up old subscriptions, and ensuring the email template is clear and includes a direct product link. The admin page should sort subscriptions by date and let merchants easily export or bulk-delete expired ones. The storefront widget must be simple and unobtrusive so it doesn't interfere with checkout flow.

plan.dataFlow: When a product's inventory changes to available, the system reads all pending subscriptions for that product and computes which customers are eligible for notification. For each eligible subscription, the system fetches the product name and storefront URL, delivers a back-in-stock email to the customer, and immediately marks the subscription as notified so any subsequent restock events for the same product are no-ops for already-notified rows. Customers subscribe via the storefront widget, which first checks their current subscription state before rendering; the widget also allows customers to cancel their own pending subscriptions, which performs a soft-delete by setting the subscription to cancelled. Merchants manage subscriptions through the admin panel, where they can cancel individual subscriptions, bulk-cancel selected entries, and physically remove already-cancelled rows as a cleanup action.

triggers.event: a product's inventory level becomes greater than zero after being out of stock
triggers.idempotency: if all subscriptions for the given product variant are already in a terminal state, treat the event as a no-op

capabilities.description: Determine whether a specific customer already has an active subscription for a given product variant.
Persist a new back-in-stock subscription for a customer and product variant.
Fetch all pending subscriptions associated with a given product variant.
Retrieve the product title and storefront URL needed to populate the notification email.
Filter the set of pending subscriptions down to those that have not yet been notified and whose email address is present.
Deliver a back-in-stock notification email to a subscribed customer including the product name and a direct link.
Transition a subscription to the notified state after the email has been successfully delivered.
Soft-delete a subscription by transitioning its status to cancelled, recording the cancellation timestamp.
Physically delete one or more subscriptions that are already in the cancelled state, as a merchant-initiated cleanup action.
Fetch a paginated, sortable list of all subscriptions for display in the merchant admin panel.
Produce a downloadable export of all subscription records for merchant reporting purposes.

persistence.name: product_subscriptions
persistence.purpose: Stores each customer's request to be notified when a specific product variant is back in stock, and tracks the lifecycle of that request.

columns.name: customer_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the customer who created the subscription

columns.name: customer_email
columns.purpose: email address to which the notification will be sent

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the parent product being watched

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the specific product variant being watched

columns.name: product_title
columns.purpose: product name captured at subscription time for email rendering without a re-fetch

columns.name: variant_title
columns.purpose: variant label captured at subscription time

columns.name: notified_at
columns.purpose: timestamp when the back-in-stock email was sent

columns.name: cancelled_at
columns.purpose: timestamp when the subscription was cancelled

persistence.keyedBy: one row per customer–variant pair; a customer may not hold more than one pending subscription for the same variant
queryPatterns: all pending subscriptions for a given product variant, used when processing a restock event
all subscriptions for a given customer and variant, used by the widget to check existing subscription state
all subscriptions ordered by creation date descending, used by the admin panel list view
all cancelled subscriptions, used by the admin bulk-removal cleanup action

transitions.trigger: back-in-stock email successfully delivered to customer
customer or merchant explicitly cancels the subscription

invariants: a row in 'notified' or 'cancelled' never returns to 'pending'
exactly one pending subscription per customer–variant pair at any time
every transition to a terminal state must record the transition timestamp in the corresponding nullable timestamp column
physical deletion via remove-subscriptions is only permitted when the row is already in the 'cancelled' state

externalContracts.purpose: Returns the current subscription state for a customer and variant so the widget renders the correct initial UI without requiring a form submission.
Creates a new pending subscription for a customer on a specific product variant.
Cancels an existing pending subscription at the customer's request, performing a soft-delete.
Returns a paginated, date-sorted list of all subscriptions for the merchant admin panel.
Cancels one or more pending subscriptions selected by the merchant, performing soft-deletes.
Physically removes subscriptions that are already in the cancelled state as a bulk cleanup action.
Produces a downloadable export of all subscription records for merchant reporting.

edgeCases: Duplicate restock event delivered for the same product variant — subscriptions already in 'notified' or 'cancelled' are excluded from processing, making re-processing a no-op.
Inventory fluctuates rapidly above and below zero — once a subscription is marked notified, it cannot revert to pending, so the customer receives at most one email per subscription.
Customer has no email address on record — skip the notification for that subscription and mark it cancelled with a recorded reason rather than leaving it stranded in pending.
Customer attempts to create a second pending subscription for the same variant — reject the request and return the existing subscription's status so the widget renders correctly.
Merchant attempts to physically remove a subscription that is still in pending state — reject the removal; the subscription must be cancelled first before physical deletion is permitted.
Restock event arrives for a product with no pending subscriptions — system performs the lookup, finds no eligible rows, and exits without performing any writes or sends.
